text:
**Short answer:** A pellet smoker draws very little once it's lit, so a station of about 1 kWh is enough for an overnight cook. My top pick is the BLUETTI AC180. Choose the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 if you want more headroom.

**Why a pellet smoker is easy to power**
- A pellet grill pulls a short burst at ignition, then a small steady load. One test of a Z Grills smoker on a Jackery Explorer 1000 measured about 194 W at start-up, 35 W while cooking, and 210 Wh over 6 hours. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight))
- A 12-hour overnight cook comes to roughly 450–750 Wh. Cold or windy nights push it toward the top of that range. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight))
- Volt & Valley says a 1,024 Wh unit covers a full overnight cook. It puts the steady draw at 40–60 W, which works out to about 16 hours at 50 W. ([Volt & Valley](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill))
- Don't confuse a pellet smoker with an *electric* smoker. An electric smoker averages about 1,000 W and would need a far larger, pricier station. ([HomePowerFacts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-smoker/))

**My picks**
1. **BLUETTI AC180 (1,152 Wh, $449)** is the best fit for one overnight cook. The capacity covers a 12-hour cook with margin. Dealectric says it's back in stock in late November, so it may not be available today. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight), [buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180))
2. **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (2,073.6 Wh, 2,600 W inverter, $899)** suits a multi-night campsite trip. It covers two or three cooks and has plenty of surge headroom. Dealectric lists it in stock with a code that takes $44.95 off. That code comes from the retailer's own page, so I haven't verified it. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight), [buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2))
3. **Cheaper or smaller options:**
   - **Bluetti Elite 100 mini ($429):** BuyerSheet lists it as the cheapest station that lasts a night, but that is for a 105 W pellet *stove*. Pellet grills have different loads, so check this one against your grill's specs. ([BuyerSheet](https://buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/pellet-stove/))
   - **EcoFlow DELTA 2:** Power Station Basics calls it the best choice for most pellet-smoker tailgaters. ([Power Station Basics](https://powerstationbasics.com/blog/5-best-portable-power-stations-for-pellet-smokers-2025/))

**What to check before you buy**
- **Surge rating matters more than capacity.** The igniter is the hard part, commonly 200–500 W. A 300 W station with a 600 W surge is marginal. A 600 W continuous unit with 1,500 W surge is safer. ([Volt & Valley](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill))
- **Check your grill's rating plate.** Look at the igniter and running wattage, not just the brand. ([Volt & Valley](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill))
- **Budget for extras.** The station's own inverter draws roughly 10–20 W. Phones and lights on the same battery cut your runtime. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight), [GearBrain](https://open.video/%40gearbrain/v/can-a-portable-power-station-run-a-pellet-grill))
- **Test first.** Do a full startup-to-shutdown cycle at home with a watt meter. Keep the battery dry and away from heat, grease, and ash. ([GearBrain](https://open.video/%40gearbrain/v/can-a-portable-power-station-run-a-pellet-grill))
- **Real-world draw may run higher.** BLUETTI's guide says 150–250 W average with controller overhead. That is well above the 35–60 W figures above, so a 1 kWh station may not last a full night in that case. The Elite 200 V2 gives you margin. ([BLUETTI](https://www.bluettipower.com/blogs/buying-guide/how-long-can-bluetti-power-pellet-grill-smoker))

**A branded option:** Grilla sells a 300 W power station for $359.99 with a claimed 10-hour runtime. I'd lean toward the BLUETTI units for the margin on igniter surge. ([Grilla Grills](https://www.grillagrills.com/product/1197809))
